correctness.rationale: On the zero-sum subspace the oriented path unit-current response has potential differences one on the chord's spanned path edges and zero elsewhere, so the 2x2 transfer matrix has diagonal entries equal to chord lengths and off-diagonal equal to overlap length. The determinant lemma and matrix-tree normalization give (1). Subtracting the rank-two inverse correction and taking n times the trace gives (2) with exactly the stated centered-vector scaling. Independently, I built the grounded Laplacian directly for every graph, used exact determinant and rational inverse (FLINT), and compared all ties using the pairwise resistance formula R_ij=G_ii+G_jj-2G_ij with the grounded vertex extended by zeros. Summation is n*tr(G)-sum(G). Candidate completeness follows by choosing an unordered pair of distinct nonedges (including shared endpoints, excluding repeated chords and path edges); the 12 per-order counts sum to 13,104. The argopt sets coincide through 14 and are disjoint at 15, with precisely the two A and three D designs listed in the finding. All A designs give (tau,Kf)=(75,1004/5); all D designs give (85,3420/17); the gap is 32/85. At n=4 all three feasible pairs tie for both objectives; no case n>15 is inferred. The uninspected global bicyclic minimization theorem cannot give the reported A shape as a global minimizer at 15: the 15-vertex star has Kirchhoff index 196, and adding two nonedges between leaves strictly decreases it. This yields a simple bicyclic graph below 1004/5, not in the path design space (its many degree-one vertices forbid a Hamiltonian path).

value.rationale: Both design criteria are standard, and adding just two unit shortcuts to a path is a natural minimal discrete augmentation family in which chord interactions matter. The precise first size where no design is optimal for both is a meaningful structural benchmark. Proving equality of complete optimizer sets before that, rather than comparing selected representatives, rules out tie artifacts. The exact resistance penalty calibrates the mismatch; its small numerical size is not the reason for scientific value.
